messages:
carlos_infra: Heads up — upgraded the eu-west GKE clusters to 1.28 overnight. Observed the gpu-dedicated node-pool unexpectedly scale down from 12 -> 3 and several GPU pods were evicted. Anyone else seeing this?

alicia_sre: yep saw same in staging, opened a watch. CA logs show it can't map nodes to nodepools after the upgrade. Short log snippet: 
```
E0522 02:12:34.123 autoscaler.go:456] NoMatchingNodePool: node 'gke-gpu-7k9' doesn't match any configured node pool labels/annotations
```

ben_platform: I think GKE changed the nodepool label in 1.28 — old label was `cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool`, new label is `topology.kubernetes.io/node-pool`. Cluster Autoscaler in our clusters is still auto-discovering by the old label. CA falls through to no-match and then treats those nodes as unmanaged so scale-down kicks in.

alicia_sre: confirmed via `kubectl get nodes -L cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool,topology.kubernetes.io/node-pool`:
```
NAME           cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool   topology.kubernetes.io/node-pool
gke-gpu-7k9    <none>                            gpu-pool-a
gke-gpu-8m2    <none>                            gpu-pool-a
```

ben_platform: ouch. Also noticed GKE now attaches an ephemeral taint `gke-node/maintenance=preemptible:NoSchedule` to some upgraded nodes temporarily during kubelet restart — combined with CA mismatch that makes GPU nodes count wrong.

eva_ml: this caused a couple ml training jobs to restart and we saw a small cost bump from emergency reprovisioning (spot -> on-demand fallbacks). Need mitigation quick for prod.

carlos_infra: any quick workaround? rollback isn't ideal across dozens of clusters.

ben_platform: short-term options:
- Patch CA command args to add auto-discovery for the new label: `--node-group-auto-discovery=label:topology.kubernetes.io/node-pool`
- Or add a tiny admission job to copy the old label into nodes to keep CA happy until we release a proper fix.
- Also set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scale-down-unready-time=20m` to be more conservative until fixed.

alicia_sre: I'm pushing a quick DaemonSet that mirrors the new label to the old label for now (read-only, only on upgraded nodes). Will apply to eu-west-prod first. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/patches/523

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/local-label-mirror -> eu-west-prod (canary: gke-gpu-7k9) :rocket:

ben_platform: I also opened a small CA patch to accept both labels when doing node discovery, so CA will match either `cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool` OR `topology.kubernetes.io/node-pool` — rolling that to canary after the label-mirror. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/134

alicia_sre: canary looks good so far, no evictions in the last 12m. scaling behavior stabilised.

carlos_infra: thanks. follow-up: we should add an upgrade test to our infra CI that verifies CA node discovery after control plane and node image upgrades — avoid blind rollouts. Filing ticket.

eva_ml: please tag the ML infra on the ticket, we want SLA guarantees during long jobs.

ben_platform: noted. I'll backport CA patch to the release branch and queue a config rollout to all regions. Will also add a prometheus alert for 'gpu-nodepool-size-drop' to catch this earlier.

carlos_infra: awesome. leaving this thread open until rollout completes. :thumbsup:
